open_points.subject: source file observation
open_points.text: Object folder → deliverer | file names, file metadata and bytes | untrusted, read only
open_points.question: What model represents an observed source file, which file-metadata facts does it contain, and is it a value snapshot or an entity that persists across scans?
options: A value snapshot minted by each scan from the name, selected metadata and observed bytes
An entity retained across scans and updated when the folder entry changes
No source-file model; name, metadata and bytes remain separate transient inputs
open_points.default_guess: Use a value snapshot minted by each scan, containing only metadata needed by stated product facts.

open_points.subject: file metadata
open_points.text: file names, file metadata and bytes
open_points.question: Which metadata items are product facts that State 1 models, rather than implementation inputs left to later states?
options: Only modification time and the camera-record facts required for the photo date
Modification time plus size, media type and other filesystem facts
All available filesystem and embedded-image metadata
No metadata is retained as a model fact
open_points.default_guess: Model only the modification time and camera-record facts required to establish the delivered photo date.

witness.initial: A source photo has a camera date different from its filesystem modification time.
events: Syncthing-fork places the photo in the object folder.
The calling flow asks the deliverer to scan the project.
outcomes: The returned source-photo value carries both observed date facts and their provenance.
The returned value carries only the selected photo date, with the observations remaining transient.
witness.observer: The calling flow and any later implementation of delivery

open_points.subject: source content identity
open_points.text: One placement exists per project and source content; repeating it changes nothing.
open_points.question: What exactly constitutes “source content,” who mints its identity, and from what evidence is that identity made?
options: The complete source byte sequence
The decoded image pixels
The prepared image after metadata removal, orientation and resizing
A caller-supplied source id
A deliverer-minted digest of the source bytes
open_points.default_guess: Treat source content as the complete observed source byte sequence and let the deliverer mint its identifier from those bytes.

witness.initial: Two files decode to identical pixels but have different EXIF blocks.
events: The owner connects a confirmed folder.
The calling flow delivers the first file.
The calling flow delivers the second file.
outcomes: A byte-based identity creates two placements.
A pixel- or prepared-image-based identity returns the first placement.
witness.observer: The calling flow and the Portal binary store

open_points.subject: source id
open_points.text:
| Calling flow → deliverer | project id, file name, source id, Portal photo id | authenticated by the deliverer's own bearer token |
| See what can be delivered for a project | each file with a status: ready, placed or published with its source id, or rejected with a reason | unknown project, unconfirmed connection or unavailable folder is refused; nothing is changed | unit tests, E2E |
open_points.question: Is a source id minted by the deliverer during scanning and later returned by the calling flow, or minted by the calling flow and merely accepted or echoed by the deliverer; and from what is it minted?
options: Deliverer-minted from source content during scan
Calling-flow-minted and supplied to every relevant operation
Externally existing identifier imported with the folder entry
Composite identity made from project id and file name
open_points.default_guess: Have the deliverer mint it from project id and source-content identity during scan, then require the caller to return it for delivery and publication recording.

witness.initial: A previously unseen file exists in a confirmed project folder.
events: The calling flow asks what can be delivered.
The deliverer returns the file and a source id.
The calling flow requests delivery using that source id.
outcomes: The source id is authoritative because the deliverer minted it from the observation.
The source id is only a caller-owned correlation value that the deliverer accepted.
witness.observer: The calling flow and the deliverer

open_points.subject: deliverable item
open_points.text: each file with a status: ready, placed or published with its source id, or rejected with a reason
open_points.question: What closed model or models represent one scan result, and which facts belong to every result versus only to particular status variants?
options: One product model with optional source id and rejection reason
A discriminated union with separate ready, placed, published and rejected variants
A source-file model plus a separate status model
Four unrelated result models
open_points.default_guess: Use a discriminated union with one variant per status and explicitly shared file identity facts.

open_points.subject: rejected item source id
open_points.text: each file with a status: ready, placed or published with its source id, or rejected with a reason
open_points.question: Does a rejected file have a source id as well as a reason, or is source id present only for ready, placed and published results?
options: Every file result, including rejected, has a source id
Only ready, placed and published results have a source id
Rejected results have a source id only when content identity could be established
open_points.default_guess: Give a rejected result a source id only when the source content could be identified; otherwise give it a separate observation identity.

witness.initial: A named file is visible but cannot be decoded as an image.
events: The calling flow scans the confirmed project folder.
The deliverer reports the file as rejected.
outcomes: The rejected result includes a stable source id that can be correlated on a later scan.
The rejected result contains only the file identity and reason, so no source id can be correlated.

open_points.subject: delivery status
open_points.text: ready, placed or published with its source id, or rejected with a reason
open_points.question: Are ready, placed, published and rejected persistent states of one entity, derived views over placement and publication records, or result variants computed independently on every scan?
options: Persistent mutable status on a source-photo entity
Derived status from immutable source, placement and publication records
Ephemeral status recomputed by each scan
open_points.default_guess: Derive status from immutable source observation, placement and publication records rather than store an independently mutable status.

open_points.subject: rejected status lifecycle
open_points.question: Is rejected terminal for a source id, or can the same file or source later become ready after replacement, completion or environmental recovery; if it can, does it retain the same identity?
options: Rejected is terminal for that source id
Rejected may become ready under the same source id
A changed file creates a new source id while transient environmental rejection can clear under the old id
open_points.default_guess: Make content rejection terminal for that source-content id, but allow environmental rejection to clear without changing the content identity.

witness.initial: A scan reports a file as rejected because its bytes are incomplete.
events: Syncthing-fork replaces the file with its complete bytes.
The calling flow scans again.
outcomes: The existing source entity changes from rejected to ready.
The complete bytes mint a new source identity while the rejected observation remains distinct.

open_points.subject: scan refusal and per-file rejection
open_points.text: unknown project, unconfirmed connection or unavailable folder is refused; nothing is changed
open_points.question: How is an action-level refusal distinguished in the model from a successful scan containing rejected file results, and does an unavailable folder yield no result collection or rejected items?
options: A separate scan-refusal result with no file items
The same result model with every affected file rejected
An exception or transport failure with no runtime model
open_points.default_guess: Use a separate typed scan-refusal result with no file items and no model mutation.

open_points.subject: failed delivery effects
open_points.text: a photo that cannot be delivered is reported with its reason and no placement is made
open_points.question: Besides forbidding a placement, may a failed delivery create or change any model such as a rejection status, delivery-attempt record, diagnostic record or cached source observation?
options: No persistent model is created or changed
A rejection/status record may be created or updated
A delivery-attempt entity is created while placement is not
Only an already existing source observation may be updated
open_points.default_guess: Create no persistent domain model on failure; return a value result containing the reason.

witness.initial: A ready source photo exists and no placement exists for it.
events: The calling flow requests delivery.
Image preparation fails.
outcomes: The operation returns a failure value and leaves all persistent models unchanged.
The operation records a failed attempt or changes the source status to rejected while creating no placement.
witness.observer: The calling flow on the next scan or retry

open_points.subject: placement
open_points.text: a prepared image in the Portal store, its reference and the publication body
open_points.question: What model is the placement, is it a value or entity, who mints it, and which source, project, prepared-image reference and publication-body facts define it?
options: A deliverer-minted entity keyed by project and source-content identity
A value identified entirely by its immutable fields
The binary-store reference itself is the placement identity
No placement model; only a delivery result exists
open_points.default_guess: Use a deliverer-minted entity whose natural uniqueness is project id plus source-content identity.

open_points.subject: prepared image
open_points.text:
A stored image carries no EXIF, GPS, XMP or comment, is upright and is at most
  2000 px on its longest side.
open_points.question: Is the prepared image a modeled value distinct from the source photo, and which stated properties and identity evidence does its model carry?
options: A value model containing content identity, dimensions, date and sanitization facts
An entity represented by the binary-store reference
Only unmodeled bytes governed by invariants
Part of the placement model with no independent identity
open_points.default_guess: Model it as an immutable value identified by its prepared bytes, with dimensions and the stated sanitization guarantees as facts.

open_points.subject: file reference
open_points.question: What does the file reference identify, who mints it, and is it a stable value, a placement entity id, or an opaque binary-store locator?
options: An opaque deliverer-minted binary-store key
The identity of the placement entity
A Portal-understood public or relative reference
A content-addressed identifier of the prepared image
open_points.default_guess: Use an opaque, credential-free binary-store key minted by the deliverer and stored as a fact of the placement.

open_points.subject: publication body
open_points.question: What model represents the publication body, which product facts does it contain, and is it an immutable value produced from the placement or a mutable entity?
options: An immutable value derived from the placement and prepared-photo facts
A mutable draft entity retained by the deliverer
An unmodeled transport payload left to contract states
A field embedded directly in the placement
open_points.default_guess: Use an immutable value produced from the placement; leave only its later encoding and wire format to later states.

open_points.subject: repeat delivery result
open_points.text: Deliver the same photo again | the first result, nothing written
open_points.question: Which persisted model is read to return “the first result,” and does sameness require returning the identical stored reference and publication-body facts or merely an equivalent newly reconstructed value?
options: Read the existing placement and return its originally stored result facts
Reconstruct an equivalent result from the existing prepared image
Store the entire first delivery-result value and return it verbatim
open_points.default_guess: Read the existing placement and return its originally stored file reference and publication body without reconstructing them.

witness.initial: A placement already exists and the rules used to construct publication bodies have since changed.
events: The calling flow delivers the same project and source content again.
outcomes: The original publication body is returned from persisted placement facts.
A newly reconstructed publication body is returned while no new placement is written.

open_points.subject: publication record
open_points.text: the file is reported as published, with its Portal photo id
open_points.question: Does recording publication create a separate publication entity, mutate the placement, or attach a Portal photo id to the source-photo entity; and who mints each identity involved?
options: Create a separate deliverer-minted publication entity linking placement and Portal photo id
Mutate the placement from placed to published
Attach publication facts to the source-photo entity
Store only a mapping from source id to Portal photo id
open_points.default_guess: Create an immutable publication record linking the existing placement to the externally minted Portal photo id, and derive published status from it.

witness.initial: A placement exists with no recorded Portal publication.
events: The calling flow creates a hidden Portal photo.
The calling flow records the returned Portal photo id with the deliverer.
outcomes: A new publication entity is created and the placement remains unchanged.
The existing placement entity changes status and gains the Portal photo id.
witness.observer: The calling flow on later scans

open_points.subject: Portal photo id
open_points.question: Is the Portal photo id modeled as an externally minted value tied to one placement, and what relation makes a later different id for the same source invalid?
options: An external value identity minted by the Portal and uniquely bound to a placement
An attribute of a mutable placement
The identity of the publication entity itself
An untyped scalar left entirely to later contracts
open_points.default_guess: Model it as a Portal-minted value identifier uniquely and immutably bound by a publication record to one placement.

open_points.subject: photo date
open_points.text:
The photo date comes from the camera record, otherwise from the file's
  modification time, and is delivered as UTC without an offset.
open_points.question: Which model owns the photo date, and does it also retain whether the value came from the camera record or file modification time?
options: The source-photo model owns the date and its provenance
The prepared-image model owns only the normalized date
The publication body owns the date with no provenance
Both source observation and prepared image carry different date facts
open_points.default_guess: Put the observed date and provenance on the source-photo value, and put the normalized delivered date on the prepared-image or publication-body value.

witness.initial: A photo has no camera date and its filesystem modification time later changes.
events: The file is scanned and delivered.
Syncthing-fork changes the file modification time without changing its bytes.
The project is scanned again.
outcomes: The original source-content identity retains the first observed photo date.
The same source-content identity now reports a different photo date derived from current metadata.
witness.observer: The calling flow and the client through the Portal
